questions.question: Factorising a trinomial is best described as:
options: Expansion run in reverse — recovering the brackets that multiplied out to give it

questions.question: For x² + 7x + 10, the two governing numbers must have:
options: Product 10 and sum 7 — the numbers 2 and 5

questions.question: The correct FIRST move on 2x² + 14x + 20 is:
options: Taking out the common factor 2, leaving 2(x² + 7x + 10), which still factorises further

questions.question: Why is factorising worth learning at all?
options: It is only needed for this one test
It makes expressions longer and more impressive
It replaces the need for arithmetic
Factors expose hidden structure — the zeros of a quadratic, the cancellations in fractions, and later the roots that calculus needs

subtopics.title: The Product-and-Sum Hunt — When a Is Not One

questions.question: For 4x² − 4x − 15, the correct target product and target sum are:
options: Product −60, sum −4, because the product is a × c when a is not one

questions.question: The target product is negative and the target sum is negative. The pair must be:
options: Opposite signs, with the larger number carrying the minus
Opposite signs, with the smaller number carrying the minus

questions.question: When the pair must have OPPOSITE signs, you hunt the factor pair whose:
options: DIFFERENCE equals the target sum's size — for −60 and −4, the pair 6 and 10

subtopics.title: Splitting the Middle Term and Grouping

questions.question: Splitting −4x as −10x + 6x is legal because:
options: Any middle term may be split into any two pieces
The exam allows one free change per question
−10x + 6x equals −4x — the value is unchanged, only the outfit
Negative terms may always be doubled

questions.question: Factoring the first pair 4x² − 10x gives:
After grouping, both pairs hold the bracket (2x − 5). This matters because:
options: It allows the brackets to cancel
It shows the trinomial is prime
The match certifies the split and signs were right, and the shared bracket can now be factored out

questions.question: Splitting in the other order, −4x = +6x − 10x, produces:
options: The same factorisation through a different route — (2x + 3)(2x − 5)
A trinomial that no longer factorises

subtopics.title: Verification, Sign Patterns and the Full Method

questions.question: Expanding (2x − 5)(2x + 3) as a check gives:
options: 4x² − 4x − 15 — the original returns, proving the factorisation

questions.question: Product a·c positive, sum negative. The pair is:
A learner factorises 4x² − 4x − 15 by hunting product −15. The museum exhibit on display is:
options: Using c instead of a × c when the leading coefficient is not one

questions.question: No factor pair passes both the product test and the sum test. The correct response is:
options: Invent a pair that is close enough
Write the trinomial as a perfect square anyway
State that the trinomial does not factorise over the integers — that statement IS the answer

subtopics.title: Two Numbers That Multiply and Add

questions.question: Two taxi fares add to R7 and multiply to 10. The fares are:
In x² + 7x + 10, the 10 and the 7 were 'born' as:
options: The 10 as a sum, the 7 as a product
The 10 as a product of the bracket numbers, the 7 as their sum

questions.question: The habit that must run BEFORE any product-and-sum hunt is:
options: Checking whether one factor divides all three terms and pulling it out front

subtopics.title: When the Number in Front Is Not a One

questions.question: For 4x² − 4x − 15, the multiply-target in the Simplifier's language is:
options: The front number times the last number: 4 × (−15) = −60

questions.question: Why does 'adding' the pair really mean 'subtracting' here?
options: Because one number is positive and the other negative, their sum is effectively a difference
Because the front number is even
Because the target is a fraction
